subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: reasoning that everyone does it [Pitfall]
passage:
On the bench outside the tea shop in the small town, after Class 10 tuition, Anand held up his phone. “Everyone's using AI for the essays. Half of 10-B. So it's fine.”
Ishita frowned. “Sir said the assignment has to be your own.”
“Sir doesn't know how many do it. If everybody does, that's basically the rule.” He liked that sentence and repeated it in his head all the way home. He pasted the prompt, submitted the answer and felt good. Then Ishita's essay, stumbling and honest, got 7 marks and his got 9 for no effort of his own, and he felt a small, unpleasant pinch. He shrugged it off. Later, when the teacher asked him to write two lines on the topic in class, he found he couldn't.

qa.q: What did Anand say about the rest of the class?
qa.a: Anand said everyone is using AI for the essays, half of 10-B.

qa.q: What might Anand's small pinch mean?
qa.a: Anand may feel uneasy and a little guilty, sensing it is not fair that his effortless answer beat Ishita's honest one.
Anand could follow the school's rule, use AI only to explain ideas and write the essay himself, since a crowd's habit does not change fairness or his own learning.

qa.q: How might Ishita feel about the marks?
qa.a: Ishita may feel frustrated or unfairly treated, since Ishita's honest work earned fewer marks than an answer with no effort.

grounding: A student argues that classmates already use AI for assignments, so it must be fine, and ignores school rules, fairness and his own skill development.
